subject: ela
cluster: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity
intro: Twelfth graders read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 11-CCR complexity band proficiently, applying all skills: multiple central ideas, strong evidence, complex interactions, word meaning, structure, author's purpose and rhetoric, and evaluating reasoning.

items.prompt:
Read.

The assembly line made goods cheap and abundant, but it also reduced skilled craftsmen to interchangeable laborers.

Name TWO central ideas.

steps: One: cheap, abundant goods. Two: the de-skilling of workers.
So the two central ideas are mass abundance and the de-skilling of labor.
solution.answer: Cheap, abundant goods and the de-skilling of labor.

items.prompt:
Read (same passage).

Name one COST mentioned.

steps: Skilled craftsmen reduced to interchangeable laborers.
So one cost was the de-skilling of craftsmen.
solution.answer: The de-skilling of craftsmen into interchangeable laborers.

items.prompt:
Read.

'We did not inherit the earth; we borrow it from our children.'

What rhetorical feature drives this line?

steps: It reframes ownership as a debt to the future, a memorable reversal.
So it uses a striking reversal/metaphor to create a sense of responsibility.
solution.answer: A striking reversal/metaphor creating a sense of responsibility to the future.

items.prompt:
